record.name: KI Norge AI safety mandate (proposed)
record.mandate: Would extend KI Norge's mandate to AI safety: capacity to evaluate AI models and to build knowledge of the consequences and risks of advanced AI, with research communities and other actors, and to give guidance on suitable models for different uses; contact point for AI Safety Institutes.

funding.description: NOK 45.1m proposed for KI Norge (budget post 28) in 2027, including the NOK 30m for model evaluation

record.mandate_short: Would add AI safety and model evaluation to KI Norge's remit.
record.notes: The budget proposal combines an AI safety mandate with a contact-point role for international safety communities, including AI Safety Institutes. It also describes guidance on risk and suitable use when choosing specific models. The counterpart route supports proposed status. Other staff figures differ: a May 2026 press report gave about ten staff, and a job advertisement offered 16 permanent posts.

agreements.counterparty: UK Government, for the UK AI Security Institute
agreements.scope: Non-binding joint statement of intent to explore cooperation, including sharing best practices between the two institutes on AI security, testing and evaluation, and exchanging knowledge of the capabilities and risks of advanced AI systems. The UK government said on 19 November 2026 that the statement creates no financial commitments and that no dedicated funding had been allocated to activities under it. Norway's government calls it a letter of intent, signed with a view to a later memorandum of understanding that sets out the cooperation in each area.
agreements.news: The two governments sign a non-binding statement of intent to explore cooperation, including between their institutes on AI security testing and evaluation.

people.name: Hans Christian Holte
people.notes: Digdir's 7 May 2026 announcement gave August 2026 as the planned start. KI Norge's article published on 1 June 2026 presents Holte as director and gives 12 June 2026 as the organisation's official launch. The additional AI safety and model-evaluation mandate remains proposed.
people.background: Holte was Director of Labour and Welfare from 2020 to 2025.

claims.text: To make KI Norge fully operational, Digdir brought technical, legal, innovation and public administration expertise together in an interim organisation from 1 December 2025.
Under the budget bill, it would be tasked in 2027 with evaluating AI models, including their safety.
Under the budget bill, it would be the contact point for international AI safety communities such as AI Safety Institutes, aiming at cooperation on methods, assessments and test tools.
Is to drive innovative and responsible development and use of AI.
Is to be established as a national arena for responsible innovation, development and use of AI.
Is to operate the national AI sandbox together with the Data Protection Authority and the Norwegian Communications Authority.
Through KI Norge, the agency has a particular responsibility to guide on, and promote, responsible and innovative use of AI in the public and private sectors.

United Kingdom-Norway Joint Statement of intent on Artificial Intelligence

excerpts.text: The ministers committed to explore collaboration in the following potential areas:
Strengthening cooperation between UK AISI and AI Norway through the sharing of best practices on AI security, testing, and evaluation, including as they relate to cybersecurity, via NCSC and NSM;
exchanging knowledge of the capabilities and risks of advanced AI systems; and exploring other opportunities for practical cooperation.
This Statement expresses the intentions of the Participants and does not create rights or obligations under international or domestic law.
Signed in Oslo on [12 November 2026], in two copies in the English language.
For the Government of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
For the Government of the Kingdom of Norway
The Statement creates no financial commitments.
No dedicated funding has been allocated to activities under the Statement.
The Norwegian Data Protection Authority (Datatilsynet)

sources.title_en: Takeoff for me, for KI Norge and for AI in Norway

excerpts.text: Vi ble etablert av regjeringen i juni i år, for å bidra til en ansvarlig og innovativ bruk av KI i Norge. Vi er en del av Digitaliseringsdirektoratet. Og – det er viktig å ha med seg: vi er per i dag 12-15 personer.
excerpts.gloss: We were established by the government in June this year to contribute to responsible and innovative use of AI in Norway. We are part of the Norwegian Digitalisation Agency. And, importantly: we are currently 12 to 15 people.

excerpts.gloss: KI Norge is to be the contact point towards international AI safety communities, for example AI Safety Institutes, with the aim of cooperation on, among other things, methods, assessments and test tools Norway cannot build up alone.

excerpts.text: Gjennom KI Noreg har direktoratet òg eit særskilt ansvar for å rettleie om, og vere ein pådrivar for ansvarleg og innovativ bruk av KI i både offentleg og privat sektor.
excerpts.gloss: Through KI Norge the directorate also has a particular responsibility to guide on, and be a driving force for, responsible and innovative use of AI in both the public and private sectors.

excerpts.text: Frå 2027 blir det foreslått å auke løyvinga med 30 mill. kroner til å styrkje KI Noreg med kapasitet til å evaluere KI-modellar, samt skaffe kunnskap om konsekvensar og risiko knytt til avansert kunstig intelligens.
excerpts.gloss: From 2027, an increase of NOK 30 million is proposed to strengthen KI Norge's capacity to evaluate AI models and obtain knowledge about the consequences and risks of advanced artificial intelligence.

excerpts.text: Datatilsynet skal fortsette samarbeidet med Digitaliseringsdirektoratet ved KI Noreg og Nasjonal kommunikasjonsmyndigheit med å etab- lere, utvikle og drifte den regulatoriske KI-sand- kassa etter KI-forordninga.
excerpts.gloss: The Data Protection Authority is to continue its cooperation with the Norwegian Digitalisation Agency, through KI Norge, and the National Communications Authority to establish, develop and run the regulatory AI sandbox under the AI Regulation.
